# NOTES ON THE TWO-BOOK TEXT (for later Q&A, in place of source)

## BOOK 1: THE ROMANCE OF GOLDEN STAR (George Griffith, 1897; Gutenberg #20173)

### Front matter
- Frontispiece: "Hail, Son of the Sun!" (p.78). Illustrator Alfred Pearse. London: F. V. White & Co., 1897.
- Epigraph: Prophecy of ancient legend of Vilcaroya-Inca and Golden Star, his sister-bride: a Son of the Sacred Race who, for Honour, Faith and Love, takes hand of a pure virgin of his own holy blood and passes with her through the Gate of Death, shall cast out the Oppressor, raise Rainbow Banner above Golden Throne of the Incas, rule the Children of the Sun.
- Contents: Prologue (I His Highness the Mummy p.1; II A Physiological Experiment p.16); Ch I Back Through the Shadows (32); II Brothers of the Blood (47); III In the Hall of Gold (66); IV The Sister Stars (86); V How Djama Did His Work (105); VI The Waking of Golden Star (124); VII In the Throne-Room of Yupanqui (145); VIII How the Soul of Golden Star Came Back (168); IX The Treachery of Djama (188); X On the Rodadero (209); XI How We Took the City of the Sun (230); XII Queen and Crown (250); XIII How Djama Paid His Debt (262); XIV The Re-kindling of the Sacred Fire (271).
- Illustrations: "Am I only dreaming that the death-sleep is over?" (p.26); "The dagger-point dropped..." (p.119); "They thrust him in with his arms still bound" (p.205); "It had smitten him to the heart" (p.228); "Now the moment for the giving of the Sign had come" (p.280).

### Prologue I – His Highness the Mummy
- Maida Vale, large old house. Professor Martin Lamson, top authority on South American antiquities, just back from a year in Peru and Bolivia with a mummy in a packing-case (7 ft x 2.5 ft).
- Dr Laurens Djama: physiologist, ~32, slender, olive skin, straight black hair, deep blue-black eyes, Eastern origin. Saved Lamson from calentura in Panama five years earlier.
- Mummy: Inca prince, early prime, dull brown long hair, aquiline features, pale bronze skin, hands crossed on breast, lying flat (unlike sitting Peruvian mummies); abdomen not eviscerated (unlike usual embalming).
- Lamson found it ~4 days' ride west of Cuzco, en route to Abancay across the Apurimac; mule lame, lost track crossing a Puna; found a circular valley with a little lake, mortarless masonry under overhanging ledge. Sent arriero Patricio away for provisions; removed stones; chamber with mummy on Vicuña skins.
- Djama proposes experiment to revive mummy in exchange for half of treasures found. Lamson agrees. Djama locks door; mentions Mephistopheles.

### Prologue II – A Physiological Experiment
- Djama's laboratory in Brondesbury Park/Kilburn garden. A week of silence. Thursday telegram: "Come round to the laboratory and make a new acquaintance who will yet be an old one."
- Mummy revived, breathing. Lamson faints. Djama's sister Ruth to be nurse; patient falsely described as from Oriental Home, Whitechapel.
- Revived Inca (Vilcaroya) speaks Quichua (Aymaru dialect). Asks for Golden Star. Lamson tells him of 1532 (365 years ago), Cajamarca, Atahuallpa captured, Huascar slain, Raymi feast, Sacred Fleece unkindled.
- Vilcaroya says Golden Star sleeps in a cave by lake; Anda-Huillac swore they'd lay her there; promises treasures.
- Dream words: "Cori-Coyllur, Nustallipa, Nusta mi!" (= "Golden Star, my princess, my darling!").

### Ch I – Back Through the Shadows
- Vilcaroya narrates: son of Huayna-Capac, prince, warrior; loved Golden Star; death-trance in Temple of the Sun bridal chamber.
- Ruth named by him "Cusi-Coyllur" (Joyful Star), after Ollantay's bride. Ruth's laugh is sweet.
- Francis Hartness: captain, ~30, tall, blue eyes, golden hair/beard; met in Panama square. Agreed to help.
- Travel: Panama → south by steamer → Arequipa (Misti, Charchani, Pichu-Pichu) → train to Sicuani → road past Cacha, Piquillacta → Cuzco plain. Vilcaroya swears vengeance on oppressors at Cuzco.

### Ch II – Brothers of the Blood
- San Sebastian village (2 leagues south of Cuzco); Ayllos descendants. Indian Ullullo (old friend). Tupac Rayca, chief, great-grandson of Tupac-Amaru (torn by horses). Vilcaroya asks in Quichua; Tupac kneels with hoe on shoulder (homage). Asks for 20 men of the Blood, meet an hour before midnight on plain behind Sacsahuaman.
- At dinner Djama hostile about Indians. Joyful Star defends them ("For shame, Laurens!").
- Hacienda 3 leagues west, price 20,000 soles (£2,000); Djama mocks; Vilcaroya insists on buying. Reveals Golden Star is his "sister". Ruth horrified: "Oh, no, no!... I will go back to England to-morrow."
- Professor explains incest taboo. Hartness: "a little reflection will show her..." Ruth leaves. Vilcaroya: "Good-night, Captain Hartness... Vilcaroya Inca is your friend."

### Ch III – In the Hall of Gold
- Vilcaroya disguises, follows Djama (Ullullo paid $10 to spy). Ullullo meeting at El Triunfo street, 11 pm.
- Route: Tullamayo rivulet, Rocca Inca, Yachahuasi, Rodadero gorge, Colcompata, Tiupunco (Gate of Sand), Rodadero pampa. Song signal. Tupac + 20 men.
- Djama blindfolded. Sayacusca (Tired Stone) cleft; pool; copper chain pulled to drain water; steps; 50 steps, right turn, measurements (10 spans, 8 spans), silver socket, slab door.
- Hall of Gold: gold plates, gold bar pyramid, Sun images with diamond eyes, ruby lips, emerald pendants. Imperial robes in copper-lidded chest (once Huascar's). Vilcaroya dresses as Inca, Llautu, Borla.
- Tupac: "Son of the Sun..." Djama sent away; Vilcaroya threatens him. Ten men fill ponchos with gold bars.
- Gold distributed; sold by professor and Djama; hacienda bought. Ruth, Joyful Star becomes housewife. Left for resting-place on 15th day.

### Ch IV – The Sister Stars
- Five-day journey: Saljantai, Umantai; Lima Tambo ruins; Apurimac bridge (Rio de la Banca); rock with three seats; twin peaks. Tunnel-door with pillar and hidden bolt (2-shilling-sized circle).
- Vilcaroya proposes Ruth view resting-place; declares not his wife, but Tupac's firstborn to wear Llautu. Ruth-Vilcaroya hands touch by lake; Vilcaroya's love for Ruth dawns; Hartness approaches.
- Golden Star's cave: Vilcaroya breaks wedge stone; fallen wall; Golden Star seen on skins. Ruth kneels; resemblance (Ruth golden hair; Golden Star black hair). Ruth kisses her brow.

### Ch V – How Djama Did His Work
- Djama alone with Golden Star for days; locked room. Vilcaroya at night sees him: Golden Star's dead-alive state; Djama says he holds her life, loves her. Demands she be his promised wife.
- Vilcaroya threatens him with dagger over Golden Star's breast. Conditions: Djama must win Golden Star's love; Djama must give Ruth to Vilcaroya. Djama agrees ("My sister for your sister"). Vilcaroya's dagger dropped on the table? (dagger fell while he dozed, vision of priests Anda-Huillac).

### Ch VI – The Waking of Golden Star
- Hartness rebukes Djama; Vilcaroya states the bargain; Ruth scolds both men ("no one can give an English girl away"). Vilcaroya yields; Djama relents, shakes hands with Vilcaroya; Golden Star wakes and kisses; first words "Cori-Coyllur Nustallipa, Nusta mi!" No memory; child's mind (17 years body).
- Ruth tells Vilcaroya to forget words. Ruth to nurse Golden Star.
- Hartness–Vilcaroya talk: Peru politically ripe for revolt; Hartness pledges to lead armies, "brothers-in-arms, rivals in love".

### Ch VII – In the Throne-Room of Yupanqui
- Ruth nurses Golden Star; Golden Star mistrusts Djama ("Evil Eyes"). Djama asks reward; Vilcaroya requires Hall-of-Gold oath; Djama wants Golden Star to go to England with Ruth for 3 years.
- Garden: Golden Star and Ruth; Golden Star cries at Djama's approach.
- Night at Rodadero picnic. Throne-room behind effigy of Yupanqui (golden mask). Ruth shown the treasure; Vilcaroya proposes to Joyful Star ("Joyful Star has taken one queen from me...").
- Tupac's men gather; Children of the Blood assemble. Footnote B on telepathic news.

### Ch VIII – How the Soul of Golden Star Came Back
- ~60 heads of families of Ayllos. Vilcaroya reveals Golden Star, marriage aside; Joyful Star as Coya (queen). Hints Hartness to be given Golden Star later. Hartness as war-leader. Golden Star wakes in memory, calls Vilcaroya "my lord"; Joyful Star kisses her; Golden Star dreams two selves.
- Djama told to forget Golden Star and go to England; Ruth to decide. Djama and professor to be blindfolded, sworn to secrecy; Djama and Lamson sent to a chamber; Hartness plans war.
- Secret exit via triangular stone; 1200 paces gallery to exit near Sayacusca. Djama and professor blindfolded and held by Ayllos.

### Ch IX – The Treachery of Djama
- Spanish officer (Governor's son Coronel Prada) with 24 Indian soldiers enters the Hall. Djama betrayed Vilcaroya to Governor Antonio Prada (who had half believed). Governor's son bound by Tupac.
- Djama shouts he would kill Vilcaroya; Vilcaroya: punish via golden cell (gold walls built by Ayllos around Djama and Spanish officer). Djama thrust in, arms bound.
- Hartness and professor; Vilcaroya gives professor choice; professor stays. Soldiers paid 2 oz gold each.

### Ch X – On the Rodadero
- Hall-of-Gold entrance flooded again; soldiers sent back with story of cave collapse.
- Ruth learns of brother's treachery; asks mercy. Golden Star loves Ruth; "Evil Eyes" gone.
- Anahuac (Ayllo) reports Governor Prada returning with 200 soldiers and dynamite to blow the Sayacusca. Night: Hartness disguised; kills sentries; Vilcaroya kills officer with knife; Hartness becomes officer of the guard.

### Ch XI – How We Took the City of the Sun
- Trap at Sayacusca: Governor and ~300 troopers lured in; water floods cleft; surrender. Hartness leads charge. Governor Prada surrenders sword to Vilcaroya at Inca's Seat.
- Cuzco fight: Gatling and Maxim machine-guns at cathedral terrace (Sub-Prefect) and Cuartel. Hartness captures guns; Cuartel taken; Cuzco won.
- Hall of Gold for soldiers' gold; Djama in cell raving.

### Ch XII – Queen and Crown
- Ruth told the story; Djama shouts from cell "Ruth, I am here!"; Ruth asks for mercy. Vilcaroya-Ruth declarations ("Your queen is not crowned yet").
- Hartness greets; Golden Star and Hartness kiss hands.
- Dawn ceremony at Sacsahuaman terrace; Rainbow Banner raised; Vilcaroya crowned Inca.

### Ch XIII – How Djama Paid His Debt
- Djama brought forward; mocks. Vilcaroya offers exile to valley. Djama rifle attack on Vilcaroya; Ullullo killed by bullet behind throne. Djama stops breathing (suicide by will); dies.

### Ch XIV – The Re-kindling of the Sacred Fire
- Conquest of empire; Lima proclamation; return to Cuzco. Church of Santo Domingo (on Temple of Sun site; footnote F).
- Feast of Raymi: Tupac-Rayca High Priest (Villac-Umu); Hartness named Viracocha; Ayllos gather. Prophecy read (repeated). Sun's sunrise ray kindles Sacred Fleece; Golden Star holds vessel; fire lit.
- Marriage-font: wine and water mixed; Vilcaroya and Joyful Star joined; Hartness and Golden Star at font next.
- Errata list: Anahauc→Anahuac, ont→out, Ullulo→Ullullo.

## BOOK 2: THE YELLOW HOUSE; MASTER OF MEN (E. Phillips Oppenheim; Gutenberg #41402; Volume One, Collier 1912)

### Principal characters
- Narrator: Kate Ffolliot, 'clergyman's daughter', lived abroad (Berlin, Heidelberg school); black hair, pale face; sharp-tongued.
- Father: Horace Ffolliot, new curate-in-charge (later Canon) at a Northshire village parish (Little parish near Deville Court); previously at Belchester; tall, slim, clean-shaven, grey eyes, fastidious.
- Alice Ffolliot: younger sister, homely, conventional, parish helper.
- Lady Amy Naselton: middle-aged matchmaker, godmother to Bruce Deville; husband; son Fred; Naselton Hall (12 miles from Sysington).
- Bruce Deville: of Deville Court; huge, untidy, beagler; ragged beard; a "failure" in Lady Naselton's view; ex-Marie Leparte patron; keeps beagles (Lawless, Marvel, Diana horse).
- Marcia / Adelaide Fortress: woman in the "Yellow House" (outside Deville Court's plantation); former journalist and Socialist; ~35-40; thin; brown hair greying; clear dark eyes; her past relationship with Horace Ffolliot (Philip Maltabar) produced Kate.
- Stephen Berdenstein: South American-returned man (Rio, ~15 years?), Berdenstein; 'Judas' in church; murdered in plantation.
- Olive Berdenstein: his sister, plain, sallow, black eyes, prominent white teeth, diamonds, sealskin coat, from Paris; loves Bruce Deville.
- Mary: maid. Morris: servant at Deville Court. Harrison: tenant farmer who set traps. Mr Charlsworth: churchwarden. Mr Hewitt: schools. Colonel Dacre: busybody. Lady Romney. Bishop of Exchester.

### Events in order
1. Ch I: Neighbourhood calls; Lady Naselton gossips about Adelaide Fortress ("Yellow House") and Bruce Deville (godson). Father reacts strongly to name "Bruce Deville"; warns daughters to avoid him.
2. Ch II: Kate sees Bruce Deville with beagles and woman (Adelaide) on lane; calls Kate "pale-faced black-haired chit". Father faints by gate, murmurs "It was her voice".
3. Ch III: Kate binds Bruce's beagle Lawless's broken leg. Father and Bruce meet; father's cold hostility; "Bruce Deville... associated with the most unhappy chapter of my life."
4. Ch IV: Kate in Yellow House during storm; Adelaide's tea; Kate learns Adelaide was Socialist; Father arrives, orders Kate out, calls Adelaide "Marcia"; they confront; "You had better go."
5. Ch V: Letter from South America to father (note "London about the 15th"); father goes to London. Bruce drops envelope: same handwriting. Bruce asks about father's train times.
6. Ch VI: Lady Naselton's tea; Berdenstein (millionaire, South America, came 3 days before; "Rio"); "Adelaide Fortress" question; he says he will surprise "her" (Adelaide); asks Kate not to tell her he's here.
7. Ch VII: Father doesn't return Friday/Saturday; Kate goes to Yellow House; Adelaide and Bruce deny knowledge; Kate reveals Berdenstein; Adelaide says father is in London. Kate sees father return with revolver ready at dusk.
8. Ch VIII: Sunday; Bishop visit; Father takes Kate walking on Bromilow Downs; meets Berdenstein walking; "Welcome to England once more, Stephen"; father leads him away.
9. Ch IX: Evening sermon "The wages of sin is death"; Berdenstein staggers into church bleeding; "Judas! you, Judas!"; dies in churchyard; Bishop: "struggling for sanctuary".
10. Ch X: Kate ill for a week; Bruce sends roses/violets; father to be canon. Inquest: murder, plantation near Yellow House.
11. Ch XI: Father admits meeting Berdenstein, says he cannot tell all; asks promise of silence. Kate frightened; moves to leave.
12. Ch XII: Olive Berdenstein visits Kate; seeks Philip Maltabar. Father refuses to see her.
13. Ch XIII: Father's wound (bandage). Kate meets Bruce at gate ("Good night, Mr. Deville").
14. Ch XIV: Father's bandage; Kate sees Bruce; Adelaide's guest Olive; "Stephen Berdenstein" ... Olive shows Maltabar photo in cabinet.
15. Ch XV–XVI: Olive's photograph of Philip Maltabar; Adelaide: it's a dead friend; Kate sees photo: it is her father. Olive: "It is Philip Maltabar."
16. Ch XVII: Bruce walks Kate home; Father reveals some information; Kate: "Marcia" is Adelaide.
17. Ch XVIII: Kate's jealousy; Olive follows Bruce; Kate and Bruce friendly; Olive at Yellow House.
18. Ch XIX: Adelaide tells Kate she is Kate's mother; father is Kate's father; the secret: Adelaide was the unmarried partner of the young Horace (Philip Maltabar); Kate is their child ("You are my child—and his!").
19. Ch XX–XXI: Kate devastated; father leaves for London; Adelaide offers Kate secretary post; Kate accepts.
20. Ch XXII: Olive's pact: Kate to avoid Bruce; Olive will drop search for Philip Maltabar.
21. Ch XXIII–XXV: Bruce walks with Kate in the plantation; Olive offers Kate ten thousand pounds to reject Bruce; Bruce proposes to Kate; Kate lies she doesn't love him.
22. Ch XXVI–XXVIII: Kate in London with Adelaide; Kate sees father in Commercial Road; father's letter from Ventnor; back in Eastminster; Bruce proposes again; they kiss.
23. Ch XXIX–XXX: Olive confronts father in study; father confesses killing Stephen Berdenstein (in self-defence, with Stephen's knife); Olive threatens police; father's farewell letter; father leaves for London; Olive follows; Kate follows with Bruce; at Colville Hall (Whitechapel) father preaches farewell to East End audience; collapses; Olive confesses she made a mistake, "I forgive. Farewell."; father: "This is happiness."

### Setting notes
- Northshire village with Yellow House, Deville Court, Naselton Hall, Sysington Hall; Bromilow Downs; Eastminster (cathedral town); Belchester (father's former parish); Exchester (diocese); Colville Hall (Whitechapel, East End); Commercial Road; Victoria Street (Adelaide's London flat); Ventnor (father's seaside retreat); Mudie's; Debenham and Freebody's; Buszard's cake.
- Dates: letter "London about fifteenth"; sermon on a Sunday; Ventnor letter dated three days before Kate's sighting.
